messages:
Anna Lopez: Quick FYI — I ran the nightly GQA+MQA perf sweep with the new paged-KV layout (kvpage v2) and saw a 12-18% tail latency regression on seqlen 512 workloads. attaching short profile below.

Raj Patel: ugh. does the regression show up for single-GPU or distributed?

Anna Lopez: single-GPU local repro first. multi-GPU looks similar but noisey.

Mike Chen: can you paste the perf counters / flame?

Anna Lopez: sure — snippet from perf top (aggregated across 1000 requests):
```
  kernel_time: attention_gqa_paged_v2         46.3%
  kernel_time: attention_mqa_shared_v1        22.5%
  memory_stalls: kv_load_hotpath              12.4%
  memcpy: kvpage_fragment_compact            6.9%
  other: scheduler_overhead                   5.1%
```

Yara Singh: kvpage_fragment_compact? we added a compaction pass in v2 to reduce fragmentation at the cost of memcpy on hotpaths. maybe that triggers for certain block sizes.

Anna Lopez: exactly. when batch seqlen histogram skews to a couple large seqs + many small ones, compaction runs more often. compaction is per-alloc right now.

Ben O'Neill: do we have the per-batch seqlen distribution logged for the sweep?

Anna Lopez: yes — here's an anonymized bucket: 
- 0-64: 420 requests
- 65-256: 310 requests
- 257-512: 270 requests
So mixed.

Raj Patel: hypothesis: compaction + the GQA paged kernel interacts poorly when blocksize is 256 vs 128. we should try forcing blocksize=128 for the kernel picker and see.

Mike Chen: +1. also check prefetch policy — the new paged kernels rely on sequential prefetching; compaction shuffles pages which defeats prefetch heuristics.

Anna Lopez: tried quick binary toggle: forcing blocksize=128 for attention_gqa_paged_v2, latency drops ~10% and memcpy falls to 2.1%. so blocksize seems correlated.

Yara Singh: then autotuner should consider (a) per-batch seqlen entropy and (b) kv_frag metric before picking paged_v2 with blocksize 256. if kv_frag > 0.3 prefer blocksize=128 or fallback to non-compacting path.

Ben O'Neill: can we add a fast kv_frag estimator to the request hotpath? maybe amortized sampling per batch (sample 4 pages) to avoid full compaction checks.

Anna Lopez: implemented a quick estimator locally — sample 8 pages for each batch; if >25% empty slots mark frag=0.4. cheap (<0.2ms) and effective.

Raj Patel: plan: (1) land estimator behind flag, (2) tweak kernel picker scoring: penalize paged_v2+bs=256 when frag>0.25 and entropy>threshold, (3) add a canary test in prod for 1% of requests.

Mike Chen: also add a perf counter to measure compaction runs/sec and percentage of requests that hit compaction. helps to set a sensible threshold.

Anna Lopez: added perf counter in local patch, will push PR with tests. attaching short diff in thread:
```
+ if (kv_frag_est > 0.25 && seqlen_entropy > 1.2) score -= 0.35; // penalize paged_v2:256
+ record_counter("kvpage/compactions_per_1k");
```

infra-bot: deploy-preview created for anna/kv-frag-autotune -> staging (tests: unit, integration, perf smoke).

Yara Singh: nice. after canary we should also log per-model thresholds — some models prefer larger blocksize due to attention kernel vectorization.

Ben O'Neill: noted — model-specific override makes sense. defaults keep safety.

Anna Lopez: thanks everyone — I'll open the PR and schedule a canary for tomorrow morning. will post results here. :thumbsup:
